Project Omega: Preliminary Combat Report  
by Head Researcher Skala, based on data gathered by Overseer Kuda  
  
The three remaining subjects of Project Omega—now designated Omega Team—had their first field test in a real combat scenario where real-time data was collected both from external readings, taken in the field by Overseer Kuda herself, as well as from the subcutaneous sensors embedded within the subjects.  
  
**Findings**  
Initial readings indicate that all three members of Omega Team have continued to show marked improvement in physical, mental, and magical power and prowess. In some instances, such improvement has created unforeseen incidences of recklessness or acute episodes of excessive displays of their newfound abilities. Of particular note, the male subjects, Plokk and Zipp, appear to be more adversely impacted by these episodes than the sole female subject, Naati, though none are unaffected.   
  
**Recommendations**  
Further study seems warranted before sending the members of Omega Team into the field again. At the very least, they should not enter combat not without adequate support from this research krewe. Overseer Kuda has taken a more direct hand in their deployment, however. Consequently, Omega Team has failed to report in for routine observation and training and appear to be accompanying her in a more supportive capacity than this researcher believes is prudent. My recommendation is that they be reassigned to Supra Fortis for further study and monitoring in a controlled setting.

The principle of the noninterventionist doctrine continues to gain ground since our doyen's fateful decision to remove our kind from the conflict against the Elder Dragons; despite leading to the schism between our people and the mursaat. 
  
That decision, and the philosophy that followed, has been met with its fair share of critics. This text will attempt to arm those who believe in this philosophical approach, so they may defend it against such rhetorical attacks. 
  
The chief rationalization that we must hold fast to is this: Sovereignty is absolute.  
  
Rather than perceiving such acts as fomenting a state of isolationism, we must understand that deciding to remain uninvolved is the ultimate act of respect for the autonomy and sovereignty of every person, culture, and society.  
  
Especially in light of the imbalance of power, which our people are in possession of, any such intervention could easily and invisibly violate the rights of another entity to espouse their innate right of self-determination.  
  
The seer people should not be in the habit of interfering in the affairs of other cultures, most especially when those cultures are objectively not as advanced or developed as our own culture has become.

Mister Keane,  

Seeing as you evaporate into thin air each time I come looking for you, I made sure this message would be delivered expressly into your hands. I know you were watching from some undisclosed shadow during Tribune Brimstone's disruption of alliance business, and I know he spoke to you afterward.  

If you're planning on joining the Castoran expedition, the Durmand Priory is owed your services. I need not remind you of your outstanding debts for books unreturned. I'm sure you believed that in the chaos of the Pact's campaign against the dragons, that record would be forgotten, lost to memory—no such luck, I'm afraid.  

With that preamble out of the way, I'll put it plainly. The Priory already has a team on location. I want you to return with the tribune and coordinate with my scholars so they can catch you up on what to expect. Deliver even one substantial artifact, and I'll consider your "loans" repaid. Or don't, and I'll see to it that General Jhavi loans you for shelving duties for the foreseeable future. Your choice.  

You can sort out the rest of your contract fees with whoever has need of you.  

Cordially,  
Steward Gixx

The most prized among two distinct types of jade, jadeite (also called imperial jade) was historically only found as transparent-to-opaque, compact, cryptocrystalline lenses, veins, or nodules deriving from natural sources.

After Shiro Tagachi's assassination of Emperor Angsiyan, the "Jade Wind" released a wave of energy that transmuted much of the surrounding organic matter into jade and petrified the forests and structures of Echovald.

This event transformed the trade in jadeite overnight, from one of scarcity and even sacredness to a highly lucrative business, as the material was ideal for a number of arcane and practical applications. This is what every Canthan knows.

However, what is not taught in our history is how Lady Joon and Xunlai Jade have manipulated the market for their own purposes and are using their so called "jade tech" to control all of us with jade para-psycho energy! They're addicting us to their—

strings.en:
**An Ethical Conundrum**

---

The presence of these chak, while an obvious impediment to our design and construction efforts to build our Navarium Core, presents our people with both an ethical and an ecological problem.

From an ethical perspective, the chak are, by all rights, a native species to this area, and as such they have at least some claim to the territory here. We are the invaders, though I know some of our kin would balk at such sentiment. Admittedly, that has never stopped the progress of any sentient species, least of all us, and the chak are no exception to that situation.

However, unlike other species that could be potentially displaced and humanely dealt with, all evidence would indicate that the chak would simply be drawn back to the ley root, like moths to a candle flame.

They literally feed on the ley root, and their very livelihood is wholly dependent on being within proximity of their food source. Mass migration of the chak would therefore be literal genocide of the species. 

There is no doubt those among us who would argue that the simplistic nature of the chak, coupled with their ferocity and polyphagia, classifies their existence as more akin to a plague than a true element of Tyria's global ecosystem. And that as such, we should not fret over such a fate.

I would argue that is reductive reasoning. While it is true that the chak behave, in many ways, more like an invasive species than anything else, the fact of the matter remains that they inhabit only those areas of the planet with the requisite concentration of ley energy to sustain their numbers.

Therefore, I believe that it is well within reason to conclude that they exist in balance with Tyria's magical ecosystem, at the very least, and possibly within the larger scope of its overarching ecological framework as well.
